definition: The enthalpy change, $\Delta H_\text{c}^\ominus$, when one mole of a substance burns completely in oxygen with all reactants and products in their standard states; it is always negative.
An exothermic reaction of a substance with oxygen, forming oxides; complete combustion of a fuel made of carbon and hydrogen (and oxygen) gives carbon dioxide and water.
Burning in a limited supply of oxygen, so some carbon forms carbon monoxide or soot (carbon) instead of carbon dioxide; carbon monoxide is toxic.

The warming of the Earth's surface and lower atmosphere because gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane absorb infrared radiation emitted by the surface and re-emit some of it back towards it.
A fuel made from recently living material, whose carbon was fixed from the air by photosynthesis; it is renewable, but not carbon neutral once farming, processing and transport are counted.
A cell that converts the chemical energy of a fuel, such as hydrogen or methanol, directly into electrical energy, with the fuel and oxygen supplied continuously.
